c: RBI Nationalised (January 1) via the RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948; Banking Regulation Act, 1949 enacted.
SBI established (July 1) by taking over the Imperial Bank of India under the State Bank of India Act, 1955.
LIC nationalised (September 1) through the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956, merging over 240 private insurers and societies.
SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act passed, bringing 8 princely state-associated banks under SBI ownership (later known as SBI Associate Banks).
14 major commercial banks nationalised (July 19) having deposits ≥ ₹50 crore under the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1969.
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) established (October 2) following the Narasimham Working Group recommendations (Prathama Bank was the first).
6 more commercial banks nationalised (April 15) having deposits ≥ ₹200 crore (Andhra Bank, Corporation Bank, New Bank of India, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Punjab & Sind Bank, Vijaya Bank).
NABARD established (July 12) under the B. Sivaraman Committee recommendations via the NABARD Act, 1981; EXIM Bank set up.
SIDBI established (April 2) as the principal financial institution for promotion and financing of MSMEs.
Narasimham Committee I report submitted, kicking off economic liberalisation, entry of private banks, and deregulation of interest rates.
First major PSB merger: New Bank of India merged into Punjab National Bank (PNB) due to financial distress, reducing nationalised banks from 20 to 19.
Mega SBI Consolidation: 5 associate banks (SBBJ, SBH, SBM, SBP, SBT) and Bharatiya Mahila Bank (BMB) merged into the State Bank of India.
Bank of Baroda Consolidation (April 1): Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank merged into Bank of Baroda.

Mega PSB Consolidation (April 1): 10 Public Sector Banks merged into 4 anchors: 1) Oriental Bank of Commerce + United Bank of India --> Punjab National Bank; 2) Syndicate Bank --> Canara Bank; 3) Andhra Bank + Corporation Bank --> Union Bank of India; 4) Allahabad Bank --> Indian Bank (Reduced the number of Public Sector Banks in India to 12)

Strategic Disinvestment & Modernisation Policy: The Central Government approved a policy framework for the potential privatisation/stake reduction of selected public sector lenders, retaining a minimum presence in strategic sectors while prioritizing digital banking units (DBUs) and PSB governance reforms.
